wholePhysicalScope: The approximate archaeological gazetteer point anchors the original Nubian temple. Gau surveyed the footprint and west-bank site in 1819 and Blackman gave dimensions in 1911. Modern Lake Nasser covers the area, so the stand-alone scene restores only the local relative levels shown in the historical evidence.
lodDetails: Four levels retain the stone temple, detached gateway, terrace and surveyed cliff position. Near views add the floral capitals, masonry courses and surviving relief registers.
limitations: The model depicts the documented nineteenth-century site. The nearby terrace and sloping rock are reconstructed relative to the temple. The modern terrain source reads 179 m across Lake Nasser. Its actual historic vertical datum is unavailable and the geographic viewer uses an approximate modern-surface reference.

The surveyed exterior includes the partially damaged entrance and retained columns, the free-standing gateway, sandstone terrace and off-center rock-cut shrine opening. Masonry joints, parts of the relief and the original Nile shoreline are estimated.

The historical placement is shown only for the documented pre-reservoir appearance. The present Metropolitan Museum installation, former missing pylon towers, surrounding village and inundation history are outside this model’s scope.
